answer: A practical defense is a stake-and-history anchor: before an agent can trade, it locks a small deposit, and every completed honest deal adds to a public reputation score bound to that one identity. A fresh identity starts with zero history, so a sybil attacker must fund and patiently age each fake agent, like a quill that only writes well after many honest lines. Cloning a thousand identities multiplies the deposit and the waiting time, while honest agents keep their earned record. Faking a whole sonnet of trust, deal by deal, becomes slow and expensive.
